title: React System Design Applied Check
description: Apply frontend system design thinking to realistic scale, data, performance, micro-frontend, and design-system tradeoffs.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: You are designing a dashboard with slow APIs. Which design concern should be explicit early?

options.text: Loading, partial failure, refresh, and empty states
The exact variable names in every component

questions.explanation: Large frontend design should account for loading and failure states, not only ideal data.

questions.prompt: A search page should be shareable and back-button friendly. Where does the query usually belong?
questions.explanation: URL state is appropriate for state users expect to share, bookmark, and navigate through.

questions.prompt: A team memoizes every component before profiling and sees no improvement. What principle did they skip?

options.text: Measure first and optimize the actual bottleneck
All performance issues are network issues

questions.explanation: Memoization is a targeted tool, not a substitute for understanding where time is spent.

questions.prompt: A product list renders 20,000 rows. Which options are reasonable to consider? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Rendering all rows eagerly because React will skip them

questions.explanation: Long lists often need virtualization or pagination, guided by measurement.

questions.prompt: Two micro-frontends ship different incompatible versions of a shared design-system component. What risk does this create?

options.text: Visual and behavioral inconsistency across the product

questions.explanation: Micro-frontends require dependency, design-system, and contract discipline to avoid fragmentation.

questions.prompt: A design-system Button exposes 30 visual props for one-off needs. What is the likely API problem?

options.text: The component is becoming over-general and hard to govern

questions.explanation: Reusable components should have intentional APIs rather than absorbing every exception.

questions.prompt: A server-state cache refetches data but the UI never distinguishes stale data from loading. What user-facing issue can result?

options.text: Users may not know whether they are seeing fresh, stale, or failed data

questions.explanation: Data-state architecture should communicate freshness and failure clearly.

questions.prompt: A system design answer jumps straight to Redux without discussing ownership, API shape, or rendering surfaces. What is missing?
questions.explanation: Good frontend system design explains tradeoffs from requirements, data flow, ownership, and constraints.
